issues.description: The template's Bitmap24 class header does not declare a default (no-argument) constructor, but the implementation file defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24() and main.cpp instantiates Bitmap24 with the default constructor. This mismatch means user code that includes the header (e.g. main.cpp) will fail to compile because the header's class declaration does not expose the default constructor even though it is implemented in the cpp file. The solution repository's header does declare the default constructor, so the template is inconsistent with the working solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Declare the default constructor in the template header to match the implementation and usage. In example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp add 'Bitmap24();' (no-argument constructor) before the existing parameterized constructor declaration so the class declaration matches the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp and the instantiation in main.cpp.
